content.content:
project's runs use the default image.

        While an image is being built for a run, the task or question shows
        "Preparing environment" as its status, and what the build prints goes
        to its raw output. A build that fails fails the run, saying why.

        The image is a Linux image, whatever the host is, so what it holds is
        installed in it for Linux, for the architecture Podman runs: each
        harness and piton at the version found on the host, from its own
        Linux release or package, never a binary copied from the host, which
        on macOS or Windows can't run in it. The build is given only the
        Containerfile the application writes for it, in a build context of
        its own, a fresh temporary directory holding nothing else, never the
        project or the user's home, and needs nothing from the host but the
        network. A version that can't be found on the host, or isn't
        published for Linux, is installed at its latest.

        Only one build of an image runs at a time. A run, a login, or a
        welcome or settings check that needs an image already being built
        waits for that build and shares how it ended, rather than starting
        another, so two builds never race to tag the same image. A build is
        tagged only once it has succeeded, so a build that fails or is
        interrupted never leaves an image that is taken for a good one, and
        the next need of it builds it again.

        A build that fails says why in Podman's own words: the step it
        failed at and everything the build printed, as written, never only
        that the image couldn't be created, and the same is kept in the log
        the application writes for its builds, beside its preferences.

    mounts:
        - "Piton", found by running `piton --version`, required, since the
            spec is built, sliced, and checked with it. Missing, its guidance
            links to https://github.com/piton-lang/piton-rs.
        - "Harness", the harness in use, as the @{HarnessIntegrationScope}
            says, found by running its command with `--version`, required,
            since Code tasks run it on the host. Missing, its guidance names the
            command and links to the harness's installation instructions,

content.text:
The build is failing because the image pins OpenCode to `opencode-ai@2.0.14`, the version read from your machine. npm doesn't have that version, so the whole install step fails, taking Claude Code and Codex down with it. I changed the spec so a bad version can't break the image, and so failures guide you instead of dumping Podman's output. `piton check` and `piton build` ran clean.

- **Versions are checked first:** each harness version taken from your machine is used only if npm confirms it exists. Otherwise that harness gets its latest version. Only a plain version number is read from the host's output.
- **One harness can't break the others:** each harness installs in its own step. One that can't install is left out and the image still builds; only runs that need it fail.
- **Version differences:** if a harness runs a different version in its container than on your machine, Welcome and Settings note it quietly, not as an error.
- **Guidance instead of walls of output:** a failure shows a short warning in plain words with fix buttons. Podman's output is collapsed under "Details" and kept in the debug log.
  - "OpenCode 2.0.14 isn't available to install", with "Use the latest OpenCode"
  - a network problem, with "Try again"
  - Podman out of disk space, with "Free up space", which runs `podman system prune` after confirming
  - anything else, with "Try again" and "Copy details"
- **Welcome uses the project's harness:** the Harness and Harness login rows name the open project's harness, so they won't say Claude Code when your project uses Codex. They re-check whenever you switch projects or change the harness.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `ContainerEnvironmentScope` `#image` and `#logging-in`; `WelcomeScope`'s Harness and Harness login checks and Check again; and `HarnessIntegrationScope` `#harnesses`.
